topicName: Adaptive Learning Rate Optimizers (AdaGrad, RMSProp, Adam, AdamW)
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Adaptive Learning Rate Optimizers (AdaGrad, RMSProp, Adam, AdamW)"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Standard Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD) uses a single learning rate for all parameter updates. However, deep learning models often feature sparse features and varying surface curvatures, making adaptive learning rate optimizers essential for faster and more reliable convergence."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. AdaGrad (Adaptive Gradient Algorithm)"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"AdaGrad adapts the learning rate per parameter by scaling it inversely proportional to the square root of the sum of all historical squared gradients. While this is great for sparse data, the accumulated squared gradients monotonically increase, often causing the learning rate to shrink prematurely and stop learning."},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"import torch
# AdaGrad optimizer in PyTorch
optimizer = torch.optim.Adagrad(model.parameters(), lr=0.01)"},{"order":6,"type":"subheading","text":"2. RMSProp (Root Mean Square Propagation)"},{"order":7,"type":"paragraph","text":"RMSProp resolves AdaGrad's radical diminishing learning rates by using an exponentially decaying average of squared gradients. This discards history from the distant past, allowing the optimizer to adapt rapidly to recent changes in the gradient geometry."},{"order":8,"type":"code","text":"import torch
# RMSProp optimizer in PyTorch
optimizer = torch.optim.RMSprop(model.parameters(), lr=0.001, alpha=0.99)"},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Adam (Adaptive Moment Estimation)"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"Adam combines the principles of both Momentum and RMSProp. It keeps track of both the exponentially decaying average of past gradients (first moment, mean) and past squared gradients (second moment, uncentered variance). Adam also incorporates bias correction terms to counteract the zero-initialization of the moment vectors."},{"order":11,"type":"code","text":"import torch
# Adam optimizer in PyTorch
optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=0.001, betas=(0.9, 0.999))"},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"4. AdamW (Adam with Decayed Weights)"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"L2 regularization and weight decay are not equivalent for adaptive gradient algorithms like Adam. AdamW decouples weight decay from the gradient updates, applying the regularization penalty directly to the weights rather than scaling it through the adaptive learning rate history. This results in significantly better generalization performance."},{"order":14,"type":"code","text":"import torch
# AdamW optimizer in PyTorch
optimizer = torch.optim.AdamW(model.parameters(), lr=0.001, weight_decay=0.01)"},{"order":15,"type":"subheading","text":"Summary of Best Practices"},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use Adam or AdamW as default starting optimizers for the vast majority of deep learning tasks due to their robust convergence properties."},{"order":17,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Prefer AdamW over standard Adam when training Transformers or models relying heavily on weight decay for regularization."},{"order":18,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Monitor validation loss closely; if training stalls due to learning rates decaying too quickly, consider switching from AdaGrad to RMSProp or Adam."}]
